brief: GS's Privorotsky argues US equities are compartmentalizing a European rates shock: OAT/Bund spreads pushed through roughly 130bp and, for the first time this episode, stress spread into BTPs, which he reads as the market pricing European sovereign risk broadly rather than French fiscal risk alone, driven by a creeping France political premium. USTs sold off hard, yet the S&P barely moved and Nasdaq and Russell finished green. On the Fed, Jefferson's call to reach the committee's 'own judgment' plus Williams argue against an automatic October hike, so October pricing has eased, though another hike later in the year stays possible. AI capex financing intensifies: AWS's fourth straight quarterly price increase, a reported Amazon Nvidia-GPU SPV, and Broadcom lending up to $42bn to its own compute customers, with circularity rising. Oil's physical system adapts to tanker attacks via alternative routes, so the durable cost shows up as a shipping/insurance premium rather than lost barrels. ISM internals show reacceleration into a supply constraint, prices paid jumping to 77.9, which is why rates aren't falling; today's NFP sweet spot is modest job growth with contained wages. He stays constructive on equities since shorts are hard to press at these real rates.
